_about: The words that must not appear in text a person reads (CLAUDE.md, Hard rules: simple enough for a child). Whole words, any case. Read by core/tests/test_plain_words.py and web/test/plain-words.test.ts, so the two lists cannot drift. Add a word only if it would actually confuse someone at the table; each needs a reason.

banned.api: a programmer's word for how programs talk to each other
banned.database: say where it is kept in plain words ("saved", "remembered")
banned.token: a programmer's word for a secret code (say "code" or "link")
banned.tokens: a programmer's word for pieces of text
banned.error code: say what went wrong and what to do
banned.exception: a programmer's word for a failure
banned.payload: a programmer's word for what a message carries
banned.endpoint: a programmer's word for an address a program calls
banned.cache: a programmer's word for a quick copy
banned.regex: a programmer's word for a pattern
banned.webhook: a programmer's word for a message another program sends
banned.oauth: the name of a sign-in method; say "sign in with Discord" or "Google"
banned.schema: a programmer's word for how data is laid out
banned.migration: a programmer's word for a data update
banned.knowledge graph: the example in CLAUDE.md: say "remembers your NPCs between sessions"
